body_text: Reservoir Media, Inc. (NASDAQ: RSVR, the “Company”), an award-winning independent music company, today announced a publishing deal with hip-hop icon T.I. Under the agreement, Reservoir will work alongside T.I. across his entire publishing catalog, spanning his back catalog and future works, including his new album, Kill the King , which debuted in the Top 10 on Billboard’s Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums and Top Rap Albums charts. Tip “T.I.” Harris, is a multi-Platinum, Grammy Award-winning artist and one of the most influential entertainers of his generation, with a career spanning music, fashion, film, and television. Widely recognized as a pioneer of Atlanta’s trap music movement, T.I. has sold over 14 million albums worldwide and has released 11 studio albums, over 100 singles, and 13 mixtapes. He has received three Grammy wins and over 60 additional industry accolades, and his extensive list of collaborators includes Jay-Z, Rihanna, Justin Timberlake, Timbaland, Eminem, Nelly, and Mariah Carey, to name a few. T.I.’s hugely successful albums include 2x-Platinum Urban Legend (2004), 2x-Platinum and #1 King (2006), Platinum and #1 T.I. vs. T.I.P. (2007), 4x-Platinum and #1 Paper Trail (2008), and more. His 2x-Platinum single “What You Know” off King won Best Rap Solo Performance at the Grammys in 2007. That same year, T.I. took home the Grammy for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration for “My Love” with Justin Timberlake off Timberlake’s FutureSex/LoveSounds . His most popular studio album, Paper Trail , featured appearances by Jay-Z, Lil Wayne, Rihanna, Justin Timberlake, and many others, and four of the album’s singles peaked within the Top Five of the Hot 100. The album features enduring rap/pop crossover hits, such as 8x-Platinum “Live Your Life” feat. Rihanna, 5x-Platinum “Dead and Gone” feat. Justin Timberlake, and Platinum “Swagga Like Us” with Jay-Z, Kanye West, and Lil Wayne. “Swagga Like Us” notably took home Best Rap Performance by a Duo or a Group at the 2009 Grammys, earning T.I. his third Grammy win. In addition to his music career, T.I. owns two successful clothing brands, has appeared in blockbuster films and hit TV shows, and is a passionate philanthropist. He founded the social justice charity “Us or Else,” which led to the release of the acclaimed socially charged compilation album entitled Us or Else: Letter to the System , featuring Reservoir roster-mate Killer Mike, plus Quavo and Meek Mill, among others. On the deal, T.I. commented, “I’m very excited about building a strong partnership with Reservoir as we work together to diversify the business and expand the reach of my catalog.” Reservoir Executive Vice President of A&R and Catalog Development Faith Newman said, “T.I. has been dubbed the ‘King of the South’ for putting Atlanta’s rap scene on the map, which helped shape the trajectory of the genre of hip-hop for the past 20 plus years. His crossover successes and enduring popularity have proven time and again how much his music resonates with fans. It’s an honor to partner with him on continuing to carve out the legacy of these cultural touchpoints he has created.” “T.I. is one of those rare powerhouses whose music has real cultural significance and staying power,” added Rell Lafargue, President and Chief Operating Officer at Reservoir. “Our focus has always been to grow our roster with world-class music, and welcoming one of rap and hip-hop’s most influential artists and bodies of work to Reservoir reinforces that mission. This partnership with T.I. also doubles down on our long-standing commitment to the genre’s storied history and promising future.” T.I. was represented on this transaction by Steven G. Shapiro and Ed Paparo of the law firm Davis, Shapiro, Lewit & Grabel, LLP.

title: 2025 State of Low-Carbon Aluminium
summary: In 2025, low-carbon aluminium is becoming a distinct and increasingly valuable commodity class.
body_text: Introduction The aluminium industry has entered a new era — one shaped as much by carbon data as by cost and quality. From expanded pricing benchmarks for low-emission products to the accelerating impact of regulations like the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), low-carbon aluminium is no longer a niche offering. In 2025, it is becoming a distinct and increasingly valuable commodity class, with its own price signals, market incentives and compliance requirements. This article explores the major developments shaping the state of low-carbon aluminium today, and what they mean for producers, traders, and buyers navigating the net-zero transition. The data: Emissions trends for primary aluminium Global trends Our raw data suggests that, on average, primary aluminium emissions intensities have decreased by 3.5% for smelter gate-to-gate emissions from 2018 to 2023. Cradle-to-gate primary aluminium emissions intensities followed the same trend, decreasing by 2.7% across the same five-year period. ‍ ‍ Scope 1 and 2 (fuel and electricity) contributions to emissions intensities at the smelter remained relatively flat across the period 2018-2023. Scope 1 contributions increased 1.5% from 68.3% to 69.8%, and scope 2 contributions decreased from 31.7% to 30.2%. Figures available in Appendix 2. The average electricity required to produce 1t of primary aluminium decreased 1.2% from 2018-2023. This is not exactly a significant decrease, revealing that the technology and practices in use within facilities have seen little improvement. However, the average grid factor applied for scope 2 electricity has dropped by over 10%. Emissions from sourcing energy/electricity appear to be on the way down, perhaps suggesting that grids are getting greener. ‍ Regional trends By region, we observed similar trends across gate-to-gate and cradle-to-gate emissions intensities for Primary Aluminium. From 2018-2023, gate-to-gate intensities trended downward significantly across Europe (by approximately 26%), North America (by approximately 21%) and Oceanic regions (by approximately 10%). Asia also showed a slight decrease (by approximately 4%). A similar trend was observed for cradle-to-gate emissions intensities. Within regions that observed a decrease, the gate-to-gate figures have decreased more than cradle-to-gate figures, and so we can conclude that the smelter intensities have decreased more significantly (in % terms) than upstream bauxite mining and alumina smelting sectors. This likely reflects more decarbonisation opportunities in primary aluminium smelting processes than those upstream processes, plus the smelting contributions (gate-to-gate intensities) are most significant to the full supply chain intensities. Low-carbon aluminium pricing expands To understand low-carbon aluminium pricing, it’s first helpful to understand LCAP (Low-Carbon Aluminium Price) and ZCAP (Zero-Carbon Aluminium Price) . LCAP and ZCAP LCAP and ZCAP are new aluminium price assessments launched by Platts (part of the S&P Global Commodity Insights) to help bring transparency to the market value of low-emission aluminium. These tools aim to support companies in navigating growing regulatory and commercial pressures around emissions — and to quantify the value of decarbonisation. The Low-Carbon Aluminium Price (LCAP) tracks a premium for aluminium with verified Scope 1 and 2 emissions of no more than 4 tonnes of CO₂ per tonne of aluminium at the smelter. This premium is assessed on top of the LME cash-settlement price and standardised to Rotterdam delivery. The Zero-Carbon Aluminium Price (ZCAP) builds on LCAP by adding the cost of offsetting any remaining emissions to zero, using Platts’ price for voluntary, aviation-grade carbon credits (CORSIA-eligible credits). The ZCAP = LCAP + (4 × CEC), where CEC is the carbon offset price on a given day. LCAP and ZCAP act as benchmarks to provide a clearer commercial signal for low- and zero-carbon aluminium, supporting low-carbon procurement decisions, improving price transparency, and creating market incentives for producers to decarbonise. LCAP and ZCAP expansion (July 2024) In July 2024, Platts expanded its European Low-Carbon Aluminium Price (LCAP) and Zero-Carbon Aluminium Price (ZCAP) assessments to provide more granular transparency for primary aluminium markets navigating decarbonisation. Previously, Platts had offered “carbon-accounted aluminium prices” — a bundled figure combining the P1020 market price with any carbon-related premium. As of July 1, Platts has unbundled these to separately publish: A clear premium for low-carbon aluminium (LCAP) over standard P1020 aluminium A separate premium for zero-carbon aluminium (ZCAP), based on the cost of offsetting the remaining emissions from low-carbon aluminium using voluntary carbon credits The move allows buyers and sellers to isolate and price the carbon-related component of aluminium more precisely, as aluminium producers and buyers can now see the actual premium being paid for lower-emissions material, separate from the baseline market price. It will also make for easier benchmarking, as smelters can better assess the commercial impact of their emissions performance and track it over time. And finally, buyers seeking low- or zero-carbon aluminium can now reference clear market-based price signals tied to verified emissions intensity. With increased regulatory pressure (e.g. CBAM) and rising demand for low-carbon materials, these updated Platts benchmarks strengthen the pricing infrastructure needed for the aluminium sector’s low-carbon transition. Platts launches daily Japan + Asia LCAP assessments Effective 2 January 2025, Platts introduced daily low-carbon aluminium premium assessments for Japan (Japan-LCAP) and Wider Asia (Asia-LCAP). These assessments mark a key shift in how the market differentiates and prices aluminium based on carbon intensity, particularly in Asian markets where demand for low-carbon commodities is rising. The move introduces transparent, region-specific carbon premiums, giving producers and buyers: A benchmark for low-carbon value recognition in Asia, similar to what exists in Europe and the US Incentive to decarbonise smelting operations, particularly for producers competing in Asia’s growing low-carbon aluminium segment Clearer commercial signals to secure premiums and differentiate low-emissions product This development reinforces the emergence of low-carbon aluminium as a tradable product class with distinct price signals. Producers with verifiable low-emissions output — especially those using renewable-powered smelting — now have a clear pathway to capture value in Asia. For aluminium buyers, the assessments support procurement strategies that align with decarbonisation goals and reporting obligations — essential as demand for climate-aligned materials grows across automotive, packaging and electronics sectors. Scrap rates for aluminium Scrap metals , especially in the aluminium industry, are gaining renewed strategic value as both a cost-saving input and a lever for reducing carbon emissions. With rising regulatory and consumer pressure to decarbonise, manufacturers are increasingly turning to scrap as a route to produce lower-carbon aluminium products — particularly in response to emissions-based mechanisms like the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). Aluminium made from scrap — especially post-consumer scrap — carries near-zero embedded emissions, since it has already fulfilled a previous life cycle. This makes it an attractive raw material under CBAM, which treats both pre-consumer and post-consumer scrap as zero-emission inputs. As a result, sourcing and using scrap can significantly lower a product’s reported carbon intensity, helping manufacturers stay competitive in carbon-regulated markets. However, the emissions implications vary depending on the type of scrap used. Internal scrap is typically excluded from carbon accounting, as it never leaves the production system. However, it does reduce waste and demand for virgin material, thereby minimising the embodied carbon of the final product. Pre-consumer scrap, created during manufacturing, presents a grey area — with different standards treating it either as a waste (zero emissions) or as a co-product (sharing emissions with final goods). While CBAM currently aligns with the former approach, this has sparked debate over potential loopholes and future regulatory tightening. Global average scrap rates for aluminium by source ‍ CBAM updates drive new trends for aluminium producers and traders Financial incentives to decarbonise The EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is already reshaping the aluminium industry — and its impact will only deepen over time. CBAM is not just a regulatory driver for emissions reporting; it’s also putting a cost on carbon. Manufacturers now have a major incentive to decarbonise. Producers whose emissions are above the threshold (expected to align with the EU’s top 10% lowest emitters) will face a cost on entry to the EU market, while those who can meet or beat that benchmark — including producers of certified low-carbon aluminium — stand to gain a commercial edge. Interest in scrap CBAM is also prompting importers to re-evaluate their supply chains, actively seeking aluminium with verified low emissions. Interest in scrap is rising sharply, since both pre- and post-consumer scrap are considered zero-emission inputs under CBAM. This could lead to increased scrap usage or, conversely, creative accounting to minimise CBAM liability. EU producers face price pressure Meanwhile, EU producers may face price pressure on exports — but globally, the market for verified low-carbon aluminium is growing as more jurisdictions explore similar border mechanisms. For producers, the message is clear: emissions data is becoming not just a reporting requirement, but a lever of competitive advantage. Greenhouse gas targets will drive transition to low-carbon aluminium At COP28, the International Aluminium Institute (IAI) launched the Aluminium Industry GHG Initiative , a global effort to standardise and track emissions reduction commitments across the sector. Backed by major aluminium producers, the initiative now aggregates corporate targets and emissions disclosures to establish an industry-wide dashboard, enhancing transparency and accountability. Key findings from the dashboard (as of January 2025): 79% of reporting companies have long-term GHG reduction targets (typically aiming for 2050 net zero) 71% have interim targets (often around 2030) 58% have committed to net-zero targets covering at least Scopes 1 and 2 Scope coverage: Most companies report Scope 1 and 2; Scope 3 reporting is increasing but not yet universal What does this tell us about the industry? 1. Corporate ambition is rising, but uneven ‍ While most leading producers (e.g. Alcoa, Hydro, Rio Tinto) have set clear emissions targets, the ambition and timelines vary. Many companies are aligning with national targets — especially in China and the Middle East — which influences the pace of action. For example, Chinese producers are relocating capacity to hydro-powered regions like Yunnan to meet national carbon peaking goals before 2030. 2. Supply chain emissions are coming into focus ‍ A growing number of companies (e.g. Hydro, Hindalco, Vedanta) are now disclosing Scope 3 emissions for their global operations, even though much of the reporting pressure for Scope 3 emissions has come from Europe. This signals increasing industry alignment with emerging regulations and buyer expectations, particularly in Europe (where mechanisms like CBAM will penalise high-carbon imports of aluminium), but also globally. 3. Data is spurring action ‍ Although targets vary, the act of publicly disclosing them — and benchmarking progress through IAI’s dashboard — has already prompted internal strategy shifts across the sector. Transparency is driving dialogue on operational decarbonisation and investment in cleaner production pathways. What does it mean for the low-carbon aluminium market? The transition to low-carbon aluminium is no longer hypothetical. Targets and disclosures are becoming prerequisites for market access, particularly in the EU. Companies with granular carbon data calculated by a verified methodology will be best placed to respond to buyer and financier scrutiny, avoid punitive default emissions values under CBAM, and even command green premiums for certified low-carbon aluminium. GHG targets are setting the foundation, but access to accurate, asset-level emissions data and proactive decarbonisation strategies will define tomorrow’s market leaders. Conclusion In 2025, the path to market access and profitability in aluminium is being redrawn by emissions intensity. Verified, asset-level data is becoming essential — not only to avoid regulatory penalties under frameworks like the EU CBAM and a potential UK CBAM, but also to unlock premiums, secure finance, and meet growing customer demand for climate-aligned products. As global pricing systems evolve and scrap becomes a strategic input, the producers and traders best positioned for success will be those who treat decarbonisation as a commercial opportunity, not just a compliance exercise. Low-carbon aluminium is here — and the market is starting to price it accordingly. ‍

title: Prove It, Don't Promise It
summary: How to tell real, incremental payment-recovery lift from an artefact of the setup. The evaluation protocol Slicker commits to being measured by.
body_text: The problem A number is not evidence by default A different customer mix, a favourable date window, a metric quietly redefined, or a rollout that favoured easy cases can all create apparent lift without the method doing anything. Before you accept a lift claim, name the ways it can be wrong. “How do I know the measured lift is real, and not an artefact of the setup?” The one question this paper answers. Recovery rate, with 95% confidence intervals Worked example from the paper: control versus Slicker on identical traffic. A chart is only the output. The evidence is the setup behind it: comparable groups, mature outcomes, and success criteria fixed before the data is seen. Confounding The two groups differ in composition, not just treatment. Hand one arm easier invoices and it outperforms for reasons that have nothing to do with the method. Selection bias Non-random assignment changes the comparison set. Letting the system opt in the cases it is likely to recover is the classic example. Regression to the mean Retry anything after a failure spike and it will appear to improve, because the spike was partly noise that was always going to subside. Cherry-picked windows A favourable fortnight can overstate performance. A test that spans one convenient calendar window inherits that window's luck. Simpson's paradox An aggregate lift can reverse inside every segment. The most counter-intuitive failure, and one that survives a casual review. None of these require intentional bias. Only an uncontrolled test. Every one has the same antidote: a design that controls composition and checks itself.

title: Isabella Bank Announces Promotion of Len Desormeau to HR Officer
summary: Isabella Bank Chief Human Resources Officer Patrick Mease announced the promotion of Len Desormeau to officer and human resources generalist.
body_text: Isabella Bank Chief Human Resources Officer Patrick Mease announced the promotion of Len Desormeau to officer and human resources generalist. In his new role, Desormeau will continue to manage the bank’s recruitment and onboarding efforts, as well as support employee relations. Desormeau’s day-to-day responsibilities include attending career fairs, overseeing the bank’s internship program and new-hire orientation process, and serving as chair of the Isabella Bank Young Professionals Network. Desormeau said he is committed to building strong relationships with staff members and expanding his knowledge of the bank and human resources trends to support key initiatives. “I see my role in human resources as someone who supports the bank’s mission by ensuring we attract, retain, and continue to develop high-performing staff members,” Desormeau said. “By doing this, I can help create an environment where staff members are motivated and dedicated to providing exceptional service to our bank customers.” Desormeau joined Isabella Bank in 2019 after beginning his career at Central Savings Bank, headquartered in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan. Over the past decade, he has worked in multiple areas of banking, with much of that time spent in human resources. Desormeau earned a bachelor’s degree in business management with a concentration in human resources from Lake Superior State University. He also completed the Dale Carnegie Comprehensive Leadership and Communication program and received the Highest Achievement Award. “This is a well-deserved promotion,” Mease said. “Len is always looking for new ways to tackle HR challenges and position himself as a trusted partner for the bank and its employees. I’m excited to see his continued growth as a leader within the organization.” Outside the office, Desormeau is active in the Mt. Pleasant community. He volunteers with organizations, including Junior Achievement, where he teaches financial literacy to local youth, and Special Olympics Michigan. He serves on the Mt. Pleasant Workforce Development Committee, is a Mt. Pleasant Area Chamber of Commerce ambassador, and served as the 2025 ambassador chair. He is also a graduate of the Mt. Pleasant Area Chamber of Commerce Rollie Denison Leadership Institute and its Capstone program. In 2025, Desormeau received the Mt. Pleasant Area Chamber of Commerce Ambassador of the Year Award. That same year, he was named among the 2025 Mid-Michigan 40 Under 40 honorees, presented by Middle Michigan Development Corp. and supported by Greater Gratiot Development Inc. Desormeau and his wife, Cali, are proud to call Mt. Pleasant home. They are parents of two children, Rhett and Sadie, and have a family dog, June. The Desormeau's enjoy cheering on local high school and college athletic teams and spending time at the area’s many parks.

title: What Is a Tax Engine? How It Works and Why Your Business Needs One
summary: Vertex is the leading and most-trusted provider of comprehensive, integrated tax technology solutions, having helped 10,000+ businesses since 1978.
body_text: Resources Library What Is a Tax Engine? How It Works and Why Your Business Needs One As tax complexity grows, businesses need a better way to apply the right tax consistently across systems, jurisdictions, and transactions. Learn how tax engines work and why they play a critical role in modern tax automation. June 24, 2019 Share Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Linkedin Share via Email What Is a Tax Engine? How It Works and Why Your Business Needs One With more than 20,000 tax jurisdictions worldwide—each with its own rates, rules, and reporting requirements that can change frequently—it can be difficult to determine the correct tax for every transaction. Determining the correct tax becomes even more challenging as your business expands. New products, new markets, and new systems often mean more tax rules to manage. What once worked in a single system can become difficult to maintain across multiple ERP, e-commerce, procurement, and financial applications. Manual processes and disconnected systems can no longer keep pace. That's why many businesses turn to a tax engine. What Is a Tax Engine? A tax engine is software that automates tax determination by calculating and applying the correct indirect tax —such as sales tax, consumer use tax, VAT, or GST—on a transaction. To do this, it evaluates information such as the product being sold, customer location, applicable tax rules, and jurisdictional requirements. Tax determination is often more complex than it appears. Take a KitKat, for example. Because it contains a wafer, some jurisdictions classify it as a baked good and apply different tax rules. Or consider a face or body lotion that contains SPF. In some locations, it may qualify for tax treatment similar to sunscreen. These kinds of nuances exist across countless products and jurisdictions. The tax applied to a purchase can vary based on what you're selling, where you're selling it, who is buying it, and the local tax rules in effect. A tax engine automatically evaluates those variables and determines the appropriate tax. How Does a Tax Engine Work? When a transaction is created in an ERP, e-commerce, procurement, or financial system, the transaction details are sent to the tax engine in real time. The tax engine evaluates information such as: Product or service type Customer information Ship-to and bill-to locations Applicable tax rules and rates Jurisdiction-specific requirements Using that information, the tax engine determines the appropriate tax and sends the calculated tax amount back to the originating system so the transaction can be completed. Tax engines are commonly integrated with ERP, e-commerce, procurement, and financial systems. Instead of maintaining tax rules and calculations separately across multiple applications, you can manage them in one place. What Are the Benefits of Using a Tax Engine? A tax engine helps simplify tax determination by centralizing tax rules and calculations in one place. Instead of managing tax across multiple systems, you can apply tax more efficiently across your business. Key benefits include: Improved tax accuracy by automatically applying the appropriate tax rules Reduced risk and audit exposure through more consistent tax determination and better visibility into tax decisions Less manual effort by automating tax calculations and reducing rework Centralized control by managing tax rules and calculations in one place Support for business growth as you expand into new markets, products, channels, and systems Whether you're responsible for tax, finance, or IT, a tax engine can help reduce manual effort, improve visibility, and create a more scalable approach to managing tax across the business. Why Getting Tax Right Upfront Matters Getting tax right at the start of a transaction matters. When tax is calculated incorrectly, the impact doesn't stop there. Errors can create additional work later in the process, leading to reporting issues, compliance challenges , audit risk, and costly corrections. The benefits of accurate tax determination extend far beyond the transaction itself. It supports reporting, audits, compliance, and broader tax and finance operations. As tax complexity grows, organizations need a reliable way to apply tax consistently and accurately across the business. Without a centralized approach to tax determination, you may face: Financial risk from underpayments, overpayments, penalties, interest assessments, and costly remediation efforts Operational inefficiencies caused by manual reviews, reconciliations, exception handling, and rework Technology challenges associated with maintaining tax logic across multiple systems and keeping tax rules up to date Reduced confidence in tax accuracy when different systems rely on different tax logic or outdated rules What Should You Look for in a Tax Engine? Not all tax engines are the same. As you evaluate solutions , consider whether they can support your business today while adapting to future growth and regulatory change. As you compare solutions, here are a few capabilities to look for: Accurate and up-to-date tax content that keeps pace with changing regulations and jurisdictional requirements. Integration with your business systems , including ERP, e-commerce, procurement, and financial applications. Centralized control of tax rules and calculations so tax can be managed consistently across your organization. Scalability to support growth , including new jurisdictions, products, channels, systems, and business models. Visibility and audit readiness , with clear reporting and insight into how tax decisions are being made. AI-enabled productivity tools that help automate complex tax tasks and improve efficiency. Support for the broader tax lifecycle , including related tax, compliance, reporting, and exemption management processes. Deployment flexibility to align with your organization's performance, security, and operational requirements. A tax engine should do more than automate calculations. It should help you create a more scalable and sustainable approach to tax determination as complexity increases. Is It Time to Invest in a Tax Engine? You may reach a point where your current approach to managing tax can no longer keep up with your business. If any of the following situations sound familiar, it may be time to evaluate whether a tax engine can help: Expanding into new regions or jurisdictions Managing tax across multiple systems or ERPs Addressing recurring audit or compliance challenges Experiencing increasing transaction volumes Preparing for ERP modernization initiatives Launching new e-commerce or digital business models If several of these challenges sound familiar, it may be a sign that your current approach to tax determination is no longer keeping pace with your business. See How Vertex Automates Tax Determination You don't need to wait until tax becomes a bottleneck before evaluating a tax engine. See how tax automation works in practice. Explore Vertex O Series to learn how you can improve tax accuracy, centralize tax determination, and scale your tax operations as complexity grows. title: Boston Event Spreads Battery Safety Awareness
summary: On July 22, in partnership with the National Waste and Recycling Association, ReSource Waste Services, and the Boston Fire Department, Casella helped host a battery take-back event in the Boston neighborhood of West Roxbury, MA.
body_text: 2026-07-27 14:04 Press release Boston Event Spreads Battery Safety Awareness On July 22, in partnership with the National Waste and Recycling Association , ReSource Waste Services, and the Boston Fire Department, Casella helped host a battery take-back event in the Boston neighborhood of West Roxbury, MA, which brought together residents, industry partners, municipal officials, and safety advocates around a simple but important goal: keeping batteries out of the trash. During the event, approximately 1,000 pounds of batteries were collected for safe recycling and proper management. Just as importantly, volunteers and organizers had dozens of meaningful conversations with community members about the growing importance of battery safety and why batteries should never be placed in household trash or recycling bins. Every battery collected represents one less potential fire risk in collection trucks, recycling facilities, and waste processing operations, while helping recover valuable materials for reuse. The batteries collected will be shipped through the Battery Network, sorted, and processed to recover as much of the recyclable material as possible. The event is another reminder that small actions can have a significant impact on public safety, environmental stewardship, and protecting the workers who keep our communities clean. To find out where to turn in your batteries and learn more about how you can help spread awareness of this growing problem, please visit www.batterysafetynow.org . Topics: Recycling Community About Casella Waste Systems, Inc. Casella Waste Systems, Inc., headquartered in Rutland, Vermont, is one of the largest recyclers and most experienced fully integrated resource management companies in the Eastern United States. Founded in 1975 as a single truck collection service, Casella has grown its operations to provide solid waste collection and disposal, transfer, recycling, and organics services to more than one million residential, commercial, municipal, institutional, and industrial customers and provides professional resource management services to over 10,000 customer locations in more than 40 states. title: What is Vendor Management? Processes, Challenges & Tools
summary: All-in-one Spend Management platform for Procure-to-Pay, Corporate Cards, Accounts Payable Automation, Vendor Payouts, Reimbursements and more!
body_text: Vendor management is about how you select, onboard, track, and work with your suppliers. Without a defined process, you risk delays, missed deadlines, compliance issues, and extra costs. A structured approach helps you stay organised, manage contracts, and measure performance more effectively. According to Gartner’s 2024 report , by 2027, 50% of companies will use AI tools to support vendor negotiations. This shows how much value businesses are placing on smarter vendor management. In this blog, you’ll learn what vendor management means, how the process works, and how the right approach can help you work more efficiently with your vendors. Key Takeaways Vendor management involves selecting, onboarding, and monitoring vendors to ensure quality and cost control. Clear communication and performance tracking help build strong vendor relationships. Technology like vendor management systems automates workflows and improves data accuracy. Common challenges include compliance risks, managing multiple vendors, and payment delays. Common challenges include handling multiple vendors, delayed payments, and regulatory risks. What Is Vendor Management? Vendor management is how you handle every part of working with your suppliers. It helps you stay in control of costs, timelines, performance, and compliance. Instead of reacting to issues, you set clear expectations from the start and track how vendors deliver over time. Here’s what vendor management typically includes: Vendor selection : Choosing the right suppliers based on price, quality, and reliability Contract management : Defining terms, timelines, and responsibilities Performance tracking : Monitoring delivery, service levels, and results Risk management : Identifying and addressing compliance or operational risks Ongoing communication : Keeping vendors aligned with your goals When done right, vendor management helps you build long-term, efficient, and accountable supplier relationships. Why Is Vendor Management Important? Without effective vendor management, your company could face delays, increased costs, and compliance issues that disrupt both daily operations and long-term growth. Here’s why managing your vendors well matters: Maintain Cost Efficiency : By negotiating competitive prices and favourable contract terms, you keep your production and operational costs under control. This directly improves your bottom line. Ensure Quality Control : Regularly monitoring vendors helps guarantee that the materials and services you receive meet your quality standards, reducing the risk of product defects or service failures. Mitigate Sourcing Risks : Identifying potential problems early—such as a vendor’s financial instability or inability to meet delivery schedules—allows you to take preventive actions, like finding alternative suppliers before disruptions occur. Stay Compliant : Vendor management ensures that your suppliers follow legal regulations and your company’s policies. This protects your business from legal risks and helps maintain industry certifications. Enable Seamless Scalability : A strong vendor management process allows your business to quickly adapt to changes in demand, whether seasonal or market-driven, ensuring uninterrupted supply and service. Improve Supply Chain Reliability : Consistent vendor oversight minimises the chances of delays or disruptions, supporting the timely delivery of goods and services. Build Strong Vendor Relationships : Effective communication and collaboration with your vendors lead to long-term partnerships, better service, and potential cost savings. Prevent Financial Errors : Keeping track of invoices and contracts helps avoid payment mistakes and contract discrepancies that could harm your financial health. Maintain Transparency and Accountability : Using regular reports and KPIs to assess vendor performance promotes transparency, helping you make informed decisions and improve supplier management. By investing in vendor management, you protect your business from risks, reduce costs, and build a dependable supply chain that supports your growth ambitions. Also Read: Vendor Relations: The Hidden Benefit of Faster Payments Vendor Management Process: Step-by-Step A structured vendor management process is essential for maintaining smooth supplier relationships and ensuring your business operates without interruptions. By following clear steps, you can select the right vendors, maintain quality and compliance, and reduce risks that could impact your operations. 1. Vendor Selection Shortlist suppliers based on more than just cost. Look for proven delivery timelines, quality standards, communication responsiveness, and financial stability. Ask for references or case studies when the stakes are high. A poor vendor at this stage becomes a bigger problem later. 2. Contract Negotiation Draft contracts that remove ambiguity. Define payment terms, delivery expectations, penalties for delays, renewal clauses, and service levels in detail. Avoid soft language. Clear terms protect both parties and reduce friction when issues arise. 3. Vendor Onboarding Collect all required documentation, such as licenses, tax information, payment instructions, and NDAs, before adding the vendor to your systems. title: Court-Appointed Monitor Finds ICE Failed to Provide Adequate Medical Care, in Violation of Court Order
summary: New report provides damning indictment of ICE’s abuses at California’s largest ICE detention center in first-ever court appointed investigation of...
body_text: Court-Appointed Monitor Finds ICE Failed to Provide Adequate Medical Care, in Violation of Court Order New report provides damning indictment of ICE’s abuses at California’s largest ICE detention center in first-ever court appointed investigation of full scope of medical care at immigration detention facility July 28, 2026 8:00 am Media Contact media@aclu.org (212) 549-2666 125 Broad Street 18th Floor New York, NY 10004 United States SAN FRANCISCO – Attorneys at the Prison Law Office, Keker, Van Nest & Peters LLP, and the American Civil Liberties Union filed a public report from a court-appointed monitor late last night that finds ICE is failing to comply with a preliminary injunction requiring it to provide a constitutionally adequate healthcare system at the California City Detention Facility. This marks the first time a court-appointed neutral party has investigated the full scope of the delivery of medical care at an ICE detention center. The report is based on a three-day site inspection, interviews with more than a dozen staff and 40 patients, and reviews of 141 patient medical records and thousands of pages of documents produced by ICE and CoreCivic, the private prison company operating the facility. The report’s findings include: Missing or incomplete medical intake screenings for existing conditions, communicable diseases, and chronic illnesses that require immediate or constant treatment Delayed and denied clinical care, including gaps in emergency care, mental health care, and specialty referrals Failure to provide timely access to prescribed medications and to identify and support patients with disabilities Inadequate staffing, incomplete training, a lack of on-site management, and insufficient clinical oversight. The external monitor concludes that access to healthcare is inadequate, making California City “an unsafe environment.” “The facility lacks a reliable system to consistently provide adequate healthcare, placing individuals at serious risk of both immediate and long-term harm,” the report states. “This pattern indicates broader problems in the facility’s health care delivery system rather than occasional lapses in care.” The report’s conclusions make clear that ICE is violating a February federal court order requiring the agency to provide adequate medical care to individuals detained at California City. Gustavo Guevara Alarcon spent nine months at the facility and experienced the conditions there firsthand. “California City failed to provide even the most basic medical care,” he said “I watched people pass out in their cells. I watched someone wait months to see an oncologist and begin lifesaving treatment. I was frequently denied basic over-the-counter medication like ibuprofen and had requests for reasonable medical accommodations repeatedly denied. No one should be subject to this kind of treatment, and certainly not at the hands of the government.” The California City Detention Facility is California’s largest ICE detention center and holds nearly 1,500 people. It is a remote facility, located in the Mojave Desert. Soon after its opening in Fall 2025, people detained at the facility sued the Trump administration and petitioned a federal court to require ICE to provide adequate medical care and improve overall conditions. In February of this year, a federal judge certified the case as a class action and granted a preliminary injunction to improve conditions for those detained at the facility. Among other things, the order required ICE to provide a functional healthcare system and appointed an external monitor for a four-month period to assess compliance and make a report and recommendations to the Court. Fernando Viera Reyes is currently being held at the California City Detention Facility. He has now been diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer, but it took five months for California City to get him a biopsy to diagnose his cancer, and another month before he was told the result. “For months, I couldn’t move, sleep, or even use the bathroom without being in extreme pain. It wasn’t until we filed this class action lawsuit and had a court order that staff at California City finally got me to a specialist. By the time I received my official diagnosis, the cancer had spread all over my body. If my ability to get cancer treatment is in the hands of this same staff, I’m scared I’ll be left without the healthcare I need. It feels like we’re being treated like we don’t have any value, but we’re all human beings, and we deserve life-saving treatment just like anyone else.” Additional quotes from Plaintiffs and co-counsel are as follows: Sokhean Keo is currently in the California City Detention Facility. “If there is no change to this system, sick people are going to die. I haven’t been able to get care for my chronic conditions because ICE refuses to work with the doctors I need to see. When I finally saw a doctor for an infection, I didn’t receive the medication they prescribed. We should be able to leave this place in one piece, not sicker than we came in.” Alejandro Mendiola Escutia has been in the California City Detention Facility for nine months. “When I arrived at California City, they confiscated my prescribed medication and the back and knee braces that were given to me by a doctor. I had to make a makeshift knee brace using my socks just to tolerate the pain. These examples just go on and on. The cruelty we’re facing is a living nightmare. We’re not asking for anything special, just asking for basic medical care." “ICE has shown time and time again that it is not putting any care into the health and safety of the people detained at the California City Detention Facility, even when explicitly required by the court,” said Carmen Iguina González, Deputy Director for Immigration Detention of the ACLU National Prison Project . “This report has made it abundantly clear that the facility is unfit to hold anyone in detention if it can’t meet their basic needs. We will continue our work to ensure that every single person detained at this facility receives the medical care they need.” “This report confirms what thousands of people have experienced firsthand: in every area of health care, California City is failing,” said Tess Borden, Managing Attorney at the Prison Law Office. “The external monitor’s findings tell a nightmarish story – psychiatric patients left without follow-up, medication and culture specimens improperly stored, specialist appointments that were missed or never scheduled. But his recommendations offer a path forward, and we’ll keep fighting for the care the Constitution demands.” “The monitor’s findings confirm that the failures at California City are hardly isolated incidents; they are systemic, ongoing, and dangerous,” Cody Harris, partner with Keker, Van Nest & Peters, said. “People detained at California City have been denied timely medical care and placed at serious risk because the facility lacks the staffing and infrastructure required to provide adequate healthcare. This conduct is especially egregious because the individuals are being held in civil detention, and the government is under court order to remedy these unconstitutional conditions.” This report can be found online here: https://www.aclu.org/documents/report-of-the-external-monitor-on-medical-care-at-california-city-detention-facility

title: The 11 Best Low-Effort Ways to Stay Social and Cool This Summer
summary: Discover low-effort indoor social activities for seniors that help reduce loneliness, support emotional well-being, and make it easier to stay connected during hot weather.
body_text: Record-breaking high temperatures have made this a challenging summer across much of the country. When the heat index stays high day after day, health experts often recommend older adults limit time outdoors to prevent dehydration, heat stroke, and falls. But that can also mean spending more time at home, feeling bored and alone. Fortunately, staying connected doesn't have to involve strenuous activities or long days in the sun. There are plenty of indoor activities for seniors that are enjoyable, low-energy, and inside where it's cool and comfortable. Keep reading for ideas on how to stay connected with friends while beating the heat this summer. Why Social Activities for Seniors Matter Research shows that maintaining friendships and participating in regular social activities supports emotional well-being, reduces feelings of loneliness , and even contributes to better physical health as we age. Having reasons to leave the house – even just once or twice a week – helps build routine, improve mood, and provide meaningful opportunities to connect with others. But if that sounds like a lot of effort, especially in the summer, we have good news. Staying social doesn't have to require lots of time or energy to reap the same sorts of benefits. 1. Meet a Friend Somewhere with AC You don't need an all-day outdoor adventure to enjoy someone's company. Meeting a friend for lunch, coffee, or even dessert can be one of the simplest summer activities for seniors. Restaurants, cafés, and diners are comfortable, air-conditioned places to sit, catch up, and enjoy a change of scenery without worrying about the heat. If afternoons are hottest where you live, consider an early lunch or mid-morning coffee date to minimize your exposure to the heat. Bonus: many local restaurants also offer early bird specials that make lunch dates more affordable. 2. Visit Your Local Senior Center If it's been a while since you've checked out your local senior center, you may be surprised by everything they have on the calendar! Many senior center activities are designed specifically for older adults looking to stay active socially without overexerting themselves in the heat, such as: Card games Bingo Craft classes Exercise classes designed for older adults Educational talks Ice cream socials Movie afternoons These programs are among the best social activities for senior citizens because everyone is open-minded to meet people, connect, and have fun. They’re designed to be welcoming, even if you're attending alone. 3. Attend Indoor Community Events Around Town Libraries, museums, churches, recreation centers, and community organizations often host free or inexpensive programs throughout the summer. And most events last only an hour or two, making them perfect for low-energy outings. Popular community indoor activities for seniors include: Book clubs Guest speakers Movie afternoons Local history presentations Craft workshops Indoor concerts Art exhibits Community game nights If you're not sure where to start, check your local library's event calendar, your city's parks and recreation department, nearby museums, community centers, places of worship, or your local newspaper's community events calendar. Many communities also have Facebook groups or neighborhood websites where upcoming events are shared. 4. Start a Weekly Coffee Tradition You don't need a special occasion to see someone! Choose one morning each week to meet the same friend, neighbor, sibling, or grandchild for coffee. Don’t like coffee? Any recurring activity works! Maybe every Tuesday evening is cookies and tea with a neighbor. Perhaps Friday becomes lunch with a sibling. Or Sunday afternoons are reserved for playing cards with friends. Small traditions remove the pressure of constantly making plans and gives you and your loved ones something to look forward to. 5. Join an Indoor Hobby Group Making friends is easier when you have something in common already, like a shared hobby. Doing a hobby in a group makes conversations flow naturally. So look for local groups for your favorite hobbies… or try something new! Some indoor hobby ideas include painting, knitting, photography, genealogy, puzzles, or board games. Chances are there's a local group that shares your interests. Even attending once a month can help you build meaningful connections over time. 6. Try Online Social Activities for Seniors Some days, it's just too hot, or you don't have the energy to leave the house. And that's perfectly okay. There are plenty of online social activities for seniors that make it easy to stay connected from home. You could: Schedule weekly video chats with family members. Join a virtual book club. Attend an online church discussion. Take an online art or history class. Play virtual trivia with friends. Even one scheduled video call each week with familiar faces can make a big difference. Check out: 9 Best Tech for Seniors Living Alone 7. Never Underestimate a Phone Call Not every social activity needs a big event or destination. Sometimes a fifteen-minute conversation is the perfect way to boost your social battery while staying cool and relaxed indoors. Calling a friend, sibling, grandchild, or former coworker can brighten your day – and theirs. Some seniors enjoy creating a rotating "phone date" schedule with friends or siblings so everyone stays in touch regularly. It's one of the lowest-effort ways to stay socially active all year long. 8. Explore Indoor Activities for Seniors with Limited Mobility Being social doesn't have to mean pushing yourself physically. There are lots of indoor activities for seniors with limited mobility, specifically designed to be comfortable and accessible. Some great options include: Chair yoga Card clubs Painting classes Puzzle groups Cooking demonstrations Music appreciation programs Movie clubs Many senior centers, libraries, and community organizations intentionally design these activities to be accessible and welcoming for people with varying mobility levels. 9. Volunteer Somewhere Air Conditioned If you're looking for a greater sense of purpose, volunteering is a wonderful option. Helping others is one of the best ways to meet people and bring more meaning to your days. You could consider: Greeting visitors at museums Assisting at food pantries Helping libraries with events Answering phones for nonprofits Hospital gift shops Community information desks Planning community events Even volunteering just a few hours each month can expand your social circle while giving back to your community. 10. Stay Connected From Home with Grow with GoGo If today’s a good day to stay home but you still want to move your body and connect with others, virtual programs are a fantastic option. Grow with GoGo offers live, instructor-led fitness classes designed specifically for older adults – that you can join from the comfort of home. Beyond the physical benefits of staying active , these classes also provide a sense of community. Seeing familiar faces each week, chatting with instructors and fellow participants, and sharing a regular routine can help make exercise feel more social and enjoyable. You’ll find classes for chair yoga, functional fitness, strength training, and more – and there’s a social period at the end of each class where everyone chats and has fun! 11. Plan One Small Outing Each Week It's easy to think you need a packed social calendar. You don't. One fun outing each week is enough to make a meaningful difference. Whether that's meeting someone for lunch, browsing a museum, or just grabbing coffee with a friend, those little moments of connection add up over time. Instead of trying to fill every day, aim for one enjoyable outing each week. That could be: Lunch with a friend A library program A museum visit A senior center class Coffee after church An indoor farmers market Visiting a shopping mall for a leisurely walk Keeping expectations small makes it much easier to stay consistent throughout the summer. Consistency with manageable activities matters more than pushing yourself at huge events. How to Stay Socially Active in Retirement Many people wonder how to stay socially active in retirement, especially if driving has become more difficult or friends have moved away. The key isn't filling your calendar with activities every day. Instead, focus on creating easy routines that fit your energy level, interests, and the season you’re in. During the hottest months of the year, that often means prioritizing indoor spaces, shorter outings, and lots of phone conversations. Try to: Schedule one social activity each week. Reach out to one friend or family member every few days. Choose indoor activities during periods of extreme heat. Join groups built around interests you already enjoy. Accept invitations, even if it's only for a short time. Small, consistent moments of connection often have a bigger impact than occasional large events. Frequently Asked Questions What are the best social activities for seniors during the summer? Some of the best summer activities for seniors include lunch with friends, senior center programs, library events, museum visits, coffee dates, volunteer opportunities, and indoor hobby groups. These activities provide opportunities for connection while still staying cool indoors. What are good indoor activities for seniors? Popular indoor activities for seniors include book clubs, card games, arts and crafts, chair exercise classes, museum visits, community lectures, movie afternoons, puzzles, and social gatherings at local senior centers. What are good indoor activities for seniors with limited mobility? Many indoor activities for seniors with limited mobility can be enjoyed while seated or with minimal walking, including painting classes, chair yoga, music groups, card clubs, puzzle clubs, cooking demonstrations, and virtual social gatherings. How can seniors stay socially active without driving? Older adults can stay connected by attending nearby community events, scheduling regular lunch dates, joining senior center programs, participating in online social activities for seniors, and using reliable transportation services like GoGo Rides to reach local outings safely and comfortably. Don’t Let “Getting There” Keep You Home Sometimes the hardest part of staying social isn't finding something to do but figuring out how to get there. If you've ever searched for social activities for seniors near me but worried about transportation, you're not alone. Many older adults stop attending events simply because they no longer drive or don't want to ask family members for rides. That's where reliable on-demand transportation for seniors can make all the difference. GoGo Rides is designed specifically to make getting out of the house easier and more comfortable. Instead of navigating an app or coordinating complicated logistics, you can simply call and request a ride to wherever you want to go, whether that's a lunch date with a friend, a senior center activity, or a community event. Because the service is built with older adults in mind, it helps remove the small barriers that add up, like remembering passwords, dealing with unfamiliar technology, or worrying about whether a ride will show up on time and be accessible for your mobility devices. Plus, GoGo Guardians are monitoring your ride every step of the way, so you always have peace of mind that you’re safe and watched out for. With dependable transportation taken care of, it becomes much easier to say “yes” to plans this summer! title: Meeting OSHA's First Aid Requirements
summary: Meeting OSHA's First Aid Requirements
body_text: Everything Employers Need to Know to Keep Their First Aid Kits Up to Standard Maintaining a well-stocked, accessible first aid kit is an essential part of workplace safety. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requires employers to ensure that first aid supplies are available and suitable for the hazards of the workplace. Depending on your industry, there are different requirements and recommendations to follow. OSHA First Aid Kit Requirements - General Workplace (Most Industries) OSHA does not mandate a specific list of first aid items for all workplaces. Instead, employers are directed to ensure "adequate first aid supplies...readily available" (29 CFR 1910.151(b)). To meet this, OSHA recognizes the ANSI/ISEA Z308.1-2021 standard as a recommended guideline for minimum first aid kit contents. Employers should assess their workplace hazards and supplement the kit as needed.

title: California Sales Tax Guide for SaaS and E-Commerce Businesses
summary: California sales & use tax guide for 2026 — rates, economic nexus, SaaS taxability, registration, and filing with the CDTFA.
body_text: California hosts many software and e-commerce companies but has one of the most complex sales tax systems in the US. Here's what you need to know about California sales tax obligations, registration requirements, and compliance. Quick Reference Item Details State Tax Rate 7.25% (6% state + 1.25% mandatory local) District Tax Range 0% - 9.5% Combined Rate Range 7.25% - 10.75% Economic Nexus $500,000 in current or previous calendar year Physical Nexus Any presence in California SaaS Taxable No (exempt as service) Registration Portal CDTFA Seller's Permit Portal Talk to a sales tax expert Get guidance tailored to your business California Sales Tax Fundamentals California imposes two complementary taxes administered by the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) : Sales tax applies to retail sales of tangible personal property within California Use tax applies to the use, consumption, or storage in California of tangible goods purchased out of state when sales tax was not charged From a remote seller's standpoint, you collect "use tax," but the rate, reporting, and payment process mirror sales tax, so this guide refers to both as sales tax. The statewide base rate is 7.25% (6% state + 1.25% mandatory local). Voter-approved district taxes can raise the combined rate to 10.75% in certain cities. Always charge the rate that applies at the customer's location. Use the CDTFA's District Tax Rate Lookup to verify current total rates by address. Tax you collect belongs to the state. Track it separately and remit it on time - penalties start at 10% of the unpaid amount. Nexus: When Are You Required to Collect? You must register, collect, and remit California sales tax once you establish nexus - a significant connection to the state. Physical nexus Triggered by any physical presence, including: Office, store, warehouse, or fulfillment center in California Employees, contractors, or sales reps working in the state Inventory stored in a California facility (e.g., Amazon FBA) Company-owned equipment or servers located in California Trade-show activity exceeding 15 days or $100,000 in sales per year Economic nexus Under Assembly Bill 147 (2019) , a remote seller has nexus if sales of tangible personal property delivered into California exceed $500,000 in the current or previous calendar year. Cross the threshold and you must register immediately. Small-seller relief: If you have no physical presence and under $500,000 in California sales, you are not required to collect. Monitor your sales so you can register promptly once you approach the limit. What Is Taxable? Category Taxable in CA? Notes Tangible personal property (clothing, electronics, home goods) Yes Default rule; exemptions are limited (most groceries, prescription drugs) SaaS (pure cloud access, no physical media) No Covered by Regulation 1502 - software accessed via the cloud is a service, not a sale of tangible goods Digital downloads (e-books, music, software) No Non-taxable when delivered electronically without a physical copy Services (consulting, custom software development) No Installation labor may be taxable if part of a product sale Bundled tangible + digital or SaaS Yes (entire bundle) Shipping any physical item can make the whole transaction taxable Rate Sourcing: Hybrid Origin/Destination Rules California uses modified-origin sourcing: State, county, and city portions follow the origin - your California place of business District taxes follow the destination - the customer's delivery address Remote sellers (economic-nexus only) apply the full destination rate, including all district taxes. Use the CDTFA's rate-lookup tool to ensure accuracy. Registering for a Seller's Permit Apply online via CDTFA's seller-permit portal Provide business details (entity type, EIN, addresses, projected sales) Registration is free, though CDTFA may request a security deposit for high-risk accounts Post the permit at any California business location Use your permit number to issue resale certificates on wholesale purchases Collecting, Filing, and Remitting Step Action Configure platforms Enable CA tax in your e-commerce or billing software. For CA-based sellers, combine origin base rate with destination district rate. Remote sellers charge full destination rate Filing frequency CDTFA assigns monthly, quarterly, or annual cadence based on tax volume File returns Report total and taxable sales, tax collected, and allocate by jurisdiction. File online through your CDTFA account Pay tax Remit electronically by the due date to avoid 10% late penalties plus interest Zero returns File even if no CA sales occurred during the period Record-keeping Retain records for at least 4 years Marketplace Facilitators Since October 1, 2019, large marketplaces (Amazon, eBay, Etsy, etc.) must collect and remit CA tax on your behalf. Their sales still count toward your $500,000 threshold. If you sell both on marketplaces and direct, register once you exceed the threshold and collect on direct sales only. Best Practices for Smooth Compliance Monitor sales against the $500,000 threshold Automate calculations - turn on the tax engine in Stripe, Shopify or any other billing platform for California if you established nexus Subscribe to CDTFA updates - local district rates change frequently Consider signing up for Afternoon.co - we can put your sales tax on autopilot Official Resources CDTFA Sales & Use Tax Overview CDTFA Seller's Permit & Registration AB 147 (2019) – Marketplace Facilitator Act CDTFA Wayfair & Remote Seller FAQ CDTFA District Tax Rate Lookup CDTFA Regulation 1502 – Computers, Programs & Data Processing CDTFA Publication 101 – Basic Sales & Use Tax CDTFA Publication 107 – Out-of-State Sellers

title: An SRE agent for production
summary: AURA is Mezmo's open-source SRE agent that runs in your infrastructure to investigate incidents, ground findings in real telemetry, and keep actions reviewable
body_text: AI has changed how software gets built. It hasn't changed how software gets run. Most of the AI money in software has gone into the IDE: code generation, copilots, developer assistants, faster pull requests. That work matters. But writing software is one slice of the lifecycle. The harder problem, and the more expensive one, is running that software in production. Production is where systems fail in ways nobody predicted. Incidents don't stay inside one service. They jump across deploys, dashboards, logs, traces, runbooks, and the on-call engineer's own judgment. When the answer is wrong in production, you don't get a failed test. You get downtime, a customer escalation, lost revenue, or a 2 a.m. page. That's the environment Mezmo built AURA for. AURA is Mezmo's SRE agent for production. It runs on your infrastructure, under your rules and your trust model, and helps SRE and platform teams investigate incidents, coordinate workflows, and move toward automation they can actually rely on, without handing over control of their data or their operational calls. Your infrastructure. Your rules. Your production SRE agent. A demo is not production It's easy to build an AI demo that looks useful. It's much harder to build an agent that holds up in production. A demo answers a clean question against a curated dataset. A production agent works inside a live system: noisy telemetry, missing context, half a dozen overlapping tools, ambiguous signals, and real risk if it gets things wrong. That raises the bar. An agent working near production can be helpful. An agent working in production has to be trusted. It has to know what it can see and what it's allowed to do. It has to leave an audit trail, behave the same way twice, and support the human on call instead of stepping around them. And it has to live inside the tools SRE teams already run. So AURA isn't a generic chatbot, a dashboard overlay, or a sealed automation layer bolted onto your stack. It's an open-source agent built for production work. The hard parts are built in Connecting an LLM to a few observability tools is the simple part. The hard parts are everything that makes an agent useful and safe once it's touching a live environment. Specialized agent workers Production incidents are rarely one step. They need investigation, a check on the findings, and a synthesis of what actually happened, sometimes a remediation plan on top of that. AURA splits an incident across specialized workers so each one reasons over the right slice of context instead of asking a single general-purpose agent to "figure it out." Grounded in real evidence A production agent can't run on vibes. AURA works from your telemetry, runbooks, service context, and incident history, not raw MCP output or whatever the model assumes is probably true. Every investigation is anchored to the evidence your team already trusts, so you get more than a plausible-sounding story. Output that checks itself AURA runs a self-checking loop: it inspects the evidence, retries when something doesn't hold up, and evaluates its findings before handing them off. Production teams don't just need an answer. They need to know the answer is supported. That step is what cuts down on shallow conclusions and confident guesses. Human-in-the-loop control Autonomy in production gets earned, not switched on. Some actions should stay advisory. Some should require a review. Some can go fully automated once your team trusts the workflow and understands how it fails. AURA keeps risky actions reviewable before they touch production, and you decide which workflows need sign-off and how far the agent can go. Earn autonomy. Don't grant it. Observable and auditable If an agent is helping run production, you need to see what it did. AURA makes the whole workflow inspectable: prompts, tool calls, decisions, the evidence it followed, and the results. Your team can trace how it reached a conclusion and what it recommended or acted on. That trail isn't there for a compliance checkbox. It's how you debug the agent and decide whether to trust it with more. SRE teams want control, not another black box SRE teams own reliability. They don't hand production access to systems they can't inspect or change, and that goes double for AI. If an agent is going to help run production, the team needs to see how it reasons, what it calls, what context it pulls, and where a human has to approve. "Turn it on and hope" isn't a plan. Trust gets built one workflow at a time. That's the whole design. AURA runs in your environment. It's open source and inspectable. You define how it works, wire it to the tools you already depend on, and set the limits on how far it's allowed to act. The point isn't to replace SRE judgment. It's to take the repetitive, reactive work off people's plates so they can spend more time designing systems that hold up on their own. From firefighter to reliability architect Good SRE teams do more than answer pages. They build the guardrails, policies, and patterns that make incidents rarer and less painful when they do happen. AI should push that shift further. AURA takes the reactive work so your team can own the proactive side: defining safe workflows, improving reliability patterns, governing what's automated, and building systems that get better over time. The role doesn't shrink. It gets more leverage. The expert doesn't disappear; the expert designs the system the agent runs inside. Why open source matters A closed SRE agent is quick to try, but it asks you to trust a black box with some of your most sensitive operational work. That's a bad trade for a lot of teams, especially the ones that want to see and change what they run. AURA is open source because a production agent should be inspectable and extensible. You can read how it works, run it in your own environment, connect it to your own tools, and adapt it to your own workflows, all while keeping control of the rules that govern how it behaves in production. The path forward Most teams are being told to "use AI." For SRE and platform teams, poking at a demo isn't the goal. You need an agent you can run on your own infrastructure, govern by your own rules, and hand real production work to. Your infrastructure. Your rules. Your production SRE agent. title: What is an EEFC Account? Meaning, Benefits, and Eligibility for Exporters
